statement: Rule-based contextual interview navigation. These are generated follow-up routes, not responses from an AI or a count of new authored atlas questions.

followupPatterns.title: A concrete episode
followupPatterns.promptTemplate:
Start with this question: {seed}
For {selfLens}, in {condition}, choose one concrete episode. What happened, in what order, and what makes this episode relevant? Keep uncertainty about dates or details visible.

followupPatterns.title: Evidence and unknowns
The three views
followupPatterns.promptTemplate:
Use this question as the anchor: {seed}
In {condition}, separate the wider available scene, what you actually noticed, and what a narrator could observe you doing. Where do the accounts diverge?

followupPatterns.title: Your meaning and correction
followupPatterns.promptTemplate:
For {seed}, consider your account so far: {previousAnswer}
What mattered to you that an observer could not know unaided? Correct one plausible misinterpretation and leave any disagreement unresolved if needed.

followupPatterns.title: A counterexample
followupPatterns.promptTemplate:
Explore the claim or preference in: {seed}
Give an episode where the opposite was true. For {selfLens}, what changed in the conditions rather than in your identity?

followupPatterns.title: Attraction repulsion and urge
followupPatterns.promptTemplate: Around {seed}, identify separately what attracts you, what repels you and what creates an urge to act. In {condition}, which of these should influence the choice, and which needs more interpretation?

followupPatterns.title: Resources and resourcefulness
followupPatterns.promptTemplate: For {seed}, describe available time, tools, people and access. Separately describe your perceived ability to use them. Change one resource condition: what becomes possible and what remains difficult?

followupPatterns.title: Competing good choices
followupPatterns.promptTemplate: Consider {seed} through {selfLens}. Name two worthwhile but competing actions. What would each make possible, cost or leave undone for you and others? What would make waiting a useful third option?

followupPatterns.title: Conditional future
followupPatterns.promptTemplate: Starting from {seed}, describe two possible good futures under different stated conditions. What would have to change, what cannot yet be known and which claim must remain an aspiration?

followupPatterns.title: Make something real
followupPatterns.promptTemplate:
Translate {seed} into an observable experiment, artifact or encounter. Use this domain task as an option: {transferTask}
State a result that would count against the idea and the permission needed before involving anyone.

followupPatterns.title: Teach and test transfer
followupPatterns.promptTemplate: Turn the insight in {seed} into a short explanation for a willing learner. What could they do in a different example to show understanding? How could they disagree with you while still demonstrating it?

followupPatterns.title: Return after life
followupPatterns.promptTemplate: Revisit {seed} after an actual action or encounter. What did you expect, what happened, what did it mean and what should change? If no action occurred, record that honestly and identify the missing condition.
